subject: testing a shiny app using testthat?

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: testing a shiny app using testthat?
parts:
As the number of lines of code in my shiny app are increasing I am trying to apply some of the suggestions on testing in Hadley Wickham's Advanced R Programming book/site (http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Testing.html). Specifically, I am trying to figure out if there is way to test (parts of) a shiny app using a script, preferably using testthat.

I have made a (very small) start (see file linked below). The first block works since most of the analyses in my app are done in regular functions. These functions are called from outputs and reactives when the app is run. For testing, however, I am using runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server)) and sink to save output from direct calls to these functions.

https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant/blob/master/inst/tests/test-regression.R

What I would really like to do is call reactives from a script and, depending on the value of input$... , see what output I get. As I wrote in the post linked below, I have an approach to load and save the state of an app that I thought would make testing easy but, unfortunately, I haven't figured out a good way to do it yet.

https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/gbLTQPjU0xQ

It would be great to hear how others test their code and if the Shiny/Rstudio folks have suggestions for best practices.

parts:
Hi Vincent,

It should be possible to interact with your app using Selenium. I installed radiant from github and had a brief play with it.
I ran radiant using runApp on R process 1. On a seperate R process I ran RSelenium.


# basic script to interact with Radiant
require(RSelenium)
port = 4678
host = "127.0.0.1"
# assume radiant is running
# for simplicity assume a second R is running
# require(radiant)
# require(shiny)
# runApp(system.file("marketing", package="radiant")
#        , host = "0.0.0.0", port = 4678)

# run checkForServer if the standalone selenium server is needed
# RSelenium::checkForServer()

startServer()
remDr <- remoteDriver$new()
Sys.sleep(20) # time for server
remDr$open()
remDr$navigate(paste0("http://", host, ":", port))
# click the navbar button
# necessary as the tab names dont seem to populate untill they are needed
webElem <- remDr$findElement(value = "//*[@class='btn btn-navbar']")
webElem$clickElement()
# get the nav-bar elements
webElem <- remDr$findElements(value = "//*[@class = 'nav']/li/a")
tabTitles <- sapply(webElem, function(x){x$getElementText()})
stateElem <- webElem[[which(tabTitles == 'State')]]

# click the state tab

stateElem$clickElement()

On clicking on the state tab the app was throwing an error:

Listening on http://0.0.0.0:4678
Error in inFile$datapath : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
Warning in is.na(x) :
  is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'

I probably need to understand how to use the app etc.
